name: A4988
full_name: DMOS Microstepping Driver with Translator and Overcurrent Protection
description: Complete microstepping motor driver with a built-in translator for easy operation of bipolar stepper motors. A single STEP pulse advances the motor one increment; DIR sets rotation. Supports full, half, quarter, eighth, and sixteenth steps, with adjustable current limiting (sense resistors + VREF), automatic mixed-decay current control, and protection including thermal shutdown, UVLO, and crossover-current protection. Operates from 8 to 35 V load supply, up to +/-2 A per phase. Supplied in a 28-lead 5x5 mm QFN with exposed thermal pad.

pins.name: OUT2B

pins.name: ENABLE
pins.description: Logic input, enables the DMOS outputs (active low)

pins.name: GND

pins.name: RESET
pins.description: Logic input; active-low reset, sets translator to home state and disables outputs

pins.name: ROSC
pins.description: Timing-set terminal; sets off-time / mixed-decay (resistor to GND, or tie to GND for fixed off-time)

pins.name: SLEEP
pins.description: Logic input; active-low sleep, minimizes power consumption

pins.name: STEP
pins.description: Logic input; rising edge advances the motor one microstep

pins.name: REF
pins.description: Gm reference voltage input (VREF) sets the current-limit threshold

pins.name: GND

pins.name: DIR

extra.thermal_pad: exposed PAD = GND, solder to ground plane

typical_application: Driving one bipolar stepper motor in 3D printers, CNC, and small automation from STEP/DIR signals with adjustable current limit.
gotchas: set the VREF current limit (Itrip = VREF / (8 x Rsense)) before running a motor or you can overheat the motor/driver
MS1/MS2/MS3 select microstep resolution; all low = full step (default), all high = 1/16 step
place a large bulk electrolytic (100 uF or more) across VBB close to the chip; supply inductance/spikes can destroy the output MOSFETs without it
on the common Pololu/generic red breakout module only ~16 of the 28 pins are broken out, and RESET and SLEEP are usually tied together (RESET must be pulled high to operate)
the QFN has an exposed thermal PAD that must be soldered to the GND plane; the GND pins (3 and 18) are only joined through it
never connect or disconnect the motor while the driver is powered, it can destroy the outputs
absolute-max load supply is 35 V; outputs swing -2 V to 37 V transiently
